remarks: This is a retry of the PB/FAL compilation. Result: NO IMPROVEMENT over the original attempt. verifiedSources count is unchanged at 1 (NSWS homepage only); excluded count increased from 11 to 21, reflecting additional candidates tried (new punjab.gov.in-family domains surfaced via fresh WebSearch, plus the indiacode.nic.in -> indiacode.gov.in migration, plus guessed NSWS sub-paths) rather than any new verified source.

pblabour.gov.in and the entire punjab.gov.in domain family (including newly-tried emapan.punjab.gov.in, fasttrack.punjab.gov.in, pbindustries.gov.in, investpunjab.gov.in, and the bare punjab.gov.in root) remain completely unreachable this session. Every attempt — bare host, www. variant, forced TLS1.2+HTTP1.1, forced TLS1.3, plain HTTP — fails identically with curl error 35 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' immediately after the TLS handshake, or (for a couple of the newer hosts) the agent-proxy relay log shows 'ws_closed_mid_exchange' (tunnel closed before the exchange completed). This is the exact same failure signature as the original attempt, strongly suggesting an unchanged, session/egress-level block on the whole punjab.gov.in domain family rather than a transient or per-page issue.

Critically, this retry's own agent-proxy status log (checked via curl $HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status before and during this session's probing) independently shows the identical 'ws_closed_mid_exchange' and 'connect_unreachable' failure pattern occurring in the same time window against a variety of OTHER states' government domains with no connection to Punjab at all — e.g. sewasetu.assam.gov.in, industries.cg.gov.in, ciflabour.assam.gov.in, rajfab.rajasthan.gov.in, labour.ap.gov.in, cglabour.nic.in, swcs.rajasthan.gov.in, singlewindow.jk.gov.in. This corroborates that the blockage is a broader, systemic issue with reaching state-government single-window/labour-department domains from this session's egress path in general, not something specific to Punjab or to any individual URL.

egazette.gov.in again fails with 'unable to get local issuer certificate' even when curl is pointed explicitly at this session's pre-trusted CA bundle (--cacert /root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt) — ruling out a simple missing-flag explanation; this looks like a genuine TLS chain issue specific to that host from this egress path.

services.india.gov.in again fails with a 502 on the CONNECT tunnel (connect_rejected per the proxy's own classification), distinct from the TLS-reset pattern seen on Punjab-family hosts; unchanged from the original attempt.

labour.gov.in/punjab-0 and the new India Code domain (indiacode.gov.in, which indiacode.nic.in now redirects to) both return HTTP 200 but are client-side-rendered application shells with empty or near-empty <body> content and no server-rendered text reachable via curl — both fall under the spec's 'empty JS-rendering shell' exclusion rather than being listed as verified sources.

Fresh WebSearch this retry session surfaced two concrete new Punjab portal names not identified in the original attempt — e-Mapan Punjab (www.emapan.punjab.gov.in, an industrial building-plan/deemed-clearance portal) and FastTrack Punjab Portal (fasttrack.punjab.gov.in, the 2025-launched industrial single-window system covering 173+ services) — both plausible and likely genuinely relevant to the factory-license process, but both are under the unreachable punjab.gov.in domain family and could not be verified this session either.

Conclusion: under unchanged network conditions, this retry does not improve on the original PB/FAL result. The one verified source remains the central NSWS homepage. The constraint is clearly network/egress-level rather than a fixable methodology issue — revisiting this state later (or from a different egress path) is the only way forward; in the meantime the original excluded-candidate URLs for pblabour.gov.in remain the best-known leads for a human to verify by other means (e.g. a browser) for the actual Punjab Factories Rules 1952 text, the factory-license process, and application forms.

Non-government sources (business-standard.com, indiafilings.com, babushahi.com, advisocompliances.blogspot.com, newsarenaindia.com, tribuneindia.com, newkerala.com, incorpx.io, thestatesman.com) continued to surface prominently in search this retry session and were excluded from candidate consideration per the spec's rule against consultancy blogs, news articles, and non-government aggregators.
